brief: A herb planter of three cells side by side, each with a bin that drains.

requirements.requirement: Herb planter of three cells side by side
requirements.evidence: Three full hex bases at (0,0,0), (1,0,0), (2,0,0) in a straight row, joined with joint bolts (lockJoints).

requirements.requirement: Each cell has a bin that drains
requirements.evidence: bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full-drain, bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full-drain, bin:2,0,0~hex-bin-full-drain (drained full-depth bins), each filled with soil and planted with basil, mint and parsley (young stage).
Props prop:1 basil-young, prop:2 mint-young, prop:3 parsley-young in the soil. check_build reports no issues, meshClash clear, no prop warnings.

finish.summary: Built a three-cell herb planter: three hex bases in a row, each with a full-depth drained bin, soil, and a young herb (basil, mint, parsley). Open faces capped and joints locked per house rules. Build checks clear. Drainage is shown by the drained bin geometry; I cannot verify water flow or material suitability.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
